indicators.note: one word grabbing another holds it inside, so the arrival encloses the place

parts.note: a comer is someone who arrives
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A newcomer takes a seat and starts scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabs' puts PUT inside COMER. 'calculating type' looks like a scheming person but is a machine that calculates.
explanation.definitionFit: A computing machine is literally a device that calculates.

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to scare someone is to alarm them

explanation.surface: An injury that sets off constant panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last E of SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A healed cut or injury leaves a mark of the same name, and the verb means to injure lastingly.

indicators.note: something embraced by another sits inside it, so the VIP word encloses the other piece

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, a social VIP
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A party host is hugged by an important guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts EG inside LION. 'Host' is not a party-giver but a great multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great crowd or army, as is a legion in the biblical 'my name is Legion'.

indicators.note: perishing suggests something falling apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A freezing wind that bites to the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perishing' reads as a description of the cold but signals an anagram of C, WIND and HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite is a light snack, and filled bread is the classic quick snack.

parts.note: read not as a casual greeting but literally: the thing that is happening, an observable event

explanation.surface: A casual greeting asking for the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: An event or occurrence that can be observed is the literal sense of the Greek word for 'that which appears'.

clue.text: Radio conking out before new charge

indicators.note: something conking out breaks down, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: The wireless breaks down ahead of a fresh bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conking out' rearranges RADIO to ORDAI, then N follows. 'charge' is a command, not a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to command or decree it, which is what ordaining does.

indicators.note: in this clue the second piece forms the base the first stands on, so they are placed one after the other

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Serious research rooted in a Mediterranean island, the clue running on into the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Something real and tangible rather than abstract is solid, substantial.

explanation.surface: Trimmed to suit a civil service office.
explanation.walkthrough: The department is Customs and Excise, the old British tax office (the page shows 'CS', most likely a misreading of 'C&E'); excise is a duty on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove surgically or edit away; Excise was the duty-collecting half of HM Customs and Excise.

clue.text: … where occasional wrecks are found, all timber and metal

parts.note: ash is a hardwood timber
ore is rock yielding metal

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: wreckage lies on the beach, all wood and iron.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7-across; the definition here describes the beach where wrecks wash up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecked ships end up on land at the coast, on the beach.

indicators.note: N is north on a compass, and not means it is removed

parts.note: to spurn is to reject or turn down

explanation.surface: A motorist is told to turn down a road but not head north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not north' removes N from SPURN. 'Drive' is the verb urge on, not motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or impel them forward.

parts.note: an incident is an occurrence or case, as in police work
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A light briefcase made of aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' is not about weight but about importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor or secondary, of little weight in importance, is merely incidental.

parts.note: reads as a remark on the temperature, but 'hot' is the slang for goods taken illegally, and this is the state they are in

explanation.surface: A remark on the sweltering weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot goods in slang are those taken by a thief.

explanation.surface: Comparing two Shakespeare heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is slang for a seducer; Othello literally killed a lady, his wife Desdemona.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser is called a Romeo, and Othello was a man who murdered a woman.

clue.text: Sailors added to tramp's first consignment

parts.note: shipmen is an old word for sailors

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Seamen are loaded onto a tramp steamer's first cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: A tramp is a cargo ship, which fits the sailors, but here it gives only T.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch of goods sent together is a consignment.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Worries about what the boss is eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' is the verb, to slim.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to cut down on food, to lose weight.

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the cleaner's title

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: What a cleaning woman most wants to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes what a charlady naturally inclines to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman's job, and so her natural tendency, is housework of this kind.

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A communion host is handed out in a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like the communion wafer but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The native faith of Japan is a religion.

clue.text: Suggestion is clear — follow with ace

indicators.note: the first piece is followed by the second, so they are placed in order

parts.note: overt means open, clear to see
an ace is the one in cards

explanation.surface: Advice that a hint is plain, so play your ace next.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied hint or suggestion, as in 'overtones of menace'.

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: puts means deposits or places
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A bank raid leaves people stunned that gold deposits were stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' reads like a robbery but turns PUTS to STUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed, stunned state is a stupor.

clue.text: Help one in fix -ie, inferior position

parts.note: to back someone is to help or support them

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so the letter sits inside the word for fix

parts.note: to set is to fix in place
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Helping someone in a jam leaves you in a lowly role.
explanation.walkthrough: '-ie' is the printed 'ie', a link word meaning 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a back seat means accepting a subordinate role.

clue.text: Wader takes a little time getting round rocky cove

indicators.note: the outer pieces get round, encircle, the rearranged word

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird takes a moment to fly round a rocky cove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' turns COVE into VOCE, and 'getting round' puts A...T around it.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-legged bird with an upturned bill is a wading bird.

explanation.surface: Something to eat inside a box.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a banger is a sausage and also a clapped-out old car, as is a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage is a food item; an old rattletrap car is called a crate.

clue.text: Happen figure in speech will prove cordial

indicators.note: in speech means the words are said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: to be is to happen, and nine is a figure, together heard as one word

explanation.surface: A speaker's numbers will turn out friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly and gentle is benign, as is cordial in the sense of warm.

clue.text: Arriving without a sign of pastrycook's utensil

indicators.note: without means outside, so the arrival word goes around the letter

parts.note: rolling in means arriving casually

indicators.note: a sign of gives only the first letter of the cook's title

explanation.surface: A pastrycook arrives lacking a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: P goes inside ROLLING IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylinder used to flatten dough is a kitchen utensil.

indicators.note: says the word for place is heard as the answer

parts.note: a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: A remark that something resembles a place name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place name' is two parts: 'place' is heard, 'name' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to mention or name as an example.

indicators.note: including means the word for horse holds the letter inside

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Grooming a horse, starting with its mane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' is not food: to curry a horse is to groom it.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to groom it with a toothed tool, as is to comb.

indicators.note: the churchman word stands outside the state abbreviation

parts.note: a dean is a senior churchman
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine

explanation.surface: A lower-ranking cleric posted outside Maine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is the verb, to degrade.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower someone in dignity is to demean or debase them.

explanation.surface: A command to fetch a big crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment is to organise strictly; a regiment of people is a great many.
